answer: Require a bond before an account can answer. Bind it to a hardware root, so one machine cannot carry ten accounts. Grade the work, then re-queue every disputed answer to a second panel drawn from a different pool. Pay per task, not per address. Trust then attaches to the delivered job rather than to the identity, and that is the bridge an operator must build before scaling, since it needs distinct hardware per account plus survival of two independent panels. Cloning keys is cheap, that bridge is not, and a farm that cannot cross it stays at the wharf with a pile of idle kernels.
